Goal: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Hypothesis to revise: TITLE: Normal-bank pseudo-masks: localising anomalies in image-labelled source data by distance to that dataset's normal patches
SUMMARY: Use the image labels of each source dataset to build a memory bank of its normal patches, mark patches of its abnormal images that are far from every normal patch as pseudo-anomalous, and train MVFA's segmentation adapters with Dice and Focal on these pseudo-masks.
HYPOTHESIS: Pseudo-masks from k-nearest-neighbour distance to a source dataset's own normal-patch bank reach at least 0.4 pixel-level IoU with true masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC training images, and segmentation adapters trained on them for all five source datasets retain at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's zero-shot pixel-AUROC margin over chance on the held-out modality.
RATIONALE: Parent 1 creates pseudo-masks from the detection branch, which reviewers doubted localises well because it is mean-pooled; parent 2 sharpens the text reference. A different source of localisation is already implicit in image labels: within one dataset, the normal images define what normal tissue looks like, so an abnormal image's patches that have no close normal neighbour are anomalous. This is MVFA's own few-shot memory-bank principle (1 - max cosine to normal patches), applied offline to the source data at scale to manufacture dense supervision for the segmentation branch.
METHOD: 1) New script make_bank_masks.py: for each source dataset, extract frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 patch tokens at the four MVFA levels for all normal training images (coreset-subsample to 10% with greedy k-center, as in PatchCore); for each abnormal training image compute per-patch score = mean over levels of (1 - max cosine to the bank); pseudo-mask = patches above the 99th percentile of the same score on held-out normal images of that dataset, restricted to the foreground (Otsu), upsampled to 240x240. 2) train_zero.py: segmentation loss = Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for every source image (normal images: empty mask); true masks are never loaded. 3) Hyper-parameters as MVFA (lr 1e-4, 50 epochs, batch size 1); coreset ratio and percentile as ablations.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; detection-to-segmentation pseudo-masks; asymmetric SigLIP-MIL. Ablations: bank features (frozen CLIP vs. adapted), percentile (97/99/99.5), coreset ratio. Metrics: pseudo-mask IoU and precision (analysis only, on datasets with masks), held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: pseudo-mask IoU below 0.25 or retention below 60%.
